hints.content: The *domain* of a function is the set of all inputs for which the function is defined.

According to the graph, $g$ is defined for all inputs between $-7$ and $4$, including both $-7$ and $4$. This means we can write the domain of $g$ as $-7 \leq x \leq 4$.

options.explanation: In most cases outside of this exercise, an image will only show part of the complete graph of a function, so unless we're given further information about the function, we will not be able to tell exactly what the domain of the function is.
options.showPrompt: Can we always tell the domain of a function from its graph?

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x- and y-axes both scale by one. The graph of the function g starts at the point negative seven, two and increases at a non linear rate to negative six, three. It continues to increase at a non linear rate to negative four, eight where it peaks and decreases at a non linear rate to zero, zero. It continues to decrease, but the rate increases to three, negative three. A line segment connects three, negative three to four, negative four, which is plotted. There is a solid horizontal line from negative seven, zero to four, zero. Both points are plotted. There is a dotted vertical line from negative seven, zero to negative seven, two. There is another dotted vertical line from four, zero to four, negative four.

hints.content: In conclusion, the domain of the function is $-7 \leq x \leq 4$.
